title: 2012 AMC 10A Problem 10
statement: Mary divides a circle into \(12\) sectors. The central angles of these sectors, measured in degrees, are all integers and they form an arithmetic sequence. What is the degree measure of the smallest possible sector angle?

solutions.text:
Let \(a\) be the smallest possible sector angle and \(d\) be the difference in the arithmetic sequence.

Then we have that \[ \dfrac{12}{2}(a + a + 11d) = 12a + 66d \] is the sum of the arithmetic sequence.

We have that this sums to \(360,\) so \[ 12a + 66d = 360 \] \[ 2a + 11d = 60. \]

We want to minimize \(a,\) so we maximize \(d.\) If \(d = 5,\) then \(a\) is not an integer, so \(d = 4\) and \(a = 8.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Use \(12a+66d=360\) and maximize \(d\) while keeping \(a\) positive
